answer: A port-economy can tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake: a new agent enters through a single inlet where it must post a bond and prove a unique compute history before trading. Reputation accrues slowly at the wharf, where peers attest to completed work, and a sybil swarm collapses because each fake identity must pay the same entry bond and earn the same slow trust — the fable of free identities dies when identity itself has a price and a past.
